messages.content:
Existing current facts about entities this note mentions:
- memory_id "1000724" [decision]: Decision on 2025-10-07: after INC-2025-023, reindex jobs will page on failure, because a silent reindex failure left stale results for two days.  (about: indexer, INC-2025-023)
- memory_id "1000721": The root cause of INC-2025-023 was a reindex job that failed silently on a full disk.  (about: indexer, INC-2025-023)
- memory_id "1000717": INC-2025-023 affected the indexer, which served stale results for two days on 2025-10-03.  (about: indexer, INC-2025-023)
- memory_id "1000401": As of 2025-05-20, the Atlas team owns the indexer, having taken it over from Cinder.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder, indexer)
- memory_id "1000345": The indexer's OpenSearch 2.11 pin lifts when the full reindex completes.  (about: indexer, OpenSearch 2.11)
- memory_id "1000341": As of 2025-04-22, the indexer is pinned to OpenSearch 2.11.  (about: indexer, OpenSearch 2.11)
- memory_id "1000154": The search indexer relies on the catalog service for product documents, so if the catalog service is down, the search indexer is down.  (about: indexer, catalog service)
- memory_id "1000331": In the catalog service, joined writes were locking product updates for seconds at a time.  (about: product catalog, catalog service)
- memory_id "1000329" [decision]: Decision on 2025-04-17: the catalog service will keep image metadata in a separate table.  (about: catalog service)
- memory_id "1000750": As of 2025-10-15, the Atlas team noticed that the image resizer's queue depth hit 50,000 after the marketing send and pinged the owners.  (about: Atlas team, image resizer)
- memory_id "1000713" [preference]: As of 2025-09-30, the Atlas team planning meeting is every Tuesday.  (about: Atlas team)
- memory_id "1000851": On 2025-12-01, the Boreal team reported that the billing API's error rate crept up to 2 percent after the dependency bump.  (about: Boreal team, billing API)
- memory_id "1000619" [constraint]: As of 2025-09-03, the catalog service (product catalog) deploys on weekdays between 08:00 and 10:00 UTC, never on Fridays.  (about: product catalog, catalog service)
- memory_id "1000729": As of 2025-10-13, the pager for the ledger service rings Cinder, not the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000831": As of 2025-11-26, the image resizer's dashboards and alerts are being repointed.  (about: image resizer)
- memory_id "1000733" [decision]: As of 2025-10-13, the ledger service is owned by Cinder, having transferred from the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, Cinder, ledger service)
- memory_id "1000690": The nightly ledger scans were blocking billing runs, which prompted the reporting service to switch from the ledger service to the bus.  (about: ledger service, billing API, the bus, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000695": As of 2025-09-23, the reporting service no longer depends on the ledger service for the nightly balance export, having switched to the bus as its source.  (about: ledger service, the bus, reporting service)
- memory_id "1000516": As of 2025-06-09, the billing API lives with the Atlas team.  (about: Atlas team, billing API)
- memory_id "1000551": As of 2025-07-30, Priya Raman is the primary on-call for the Atlas team, taking over from Tomasz.  (about: Atlas team, Priya Raman, Tomasz)
Existing entity names: indexer, INC-2025-023, Atlas team, Cinder, OpenSearch 2.11, catalog service, product catalog, image resizer, Boreal team, billing API, ledger service, the bus, reporting service, Priya Raman, Tomasz

The note:

[2025-12-18] standup/atlas/2025-12-18: Decided in today's standup: search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, since incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes.

message.reasoning:
Let me analyze this note.

The note: "[2025-12-18] standup/atlas/2025-12-18: Decided in today's standup: search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, since incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes."

Entities mentioned: "search-indexer" — this is likely an alias for "indexer" (existing entity). The note says "search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write".

This is a decision: the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, because incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes.

New facts:
- Decision on 2025-12-18: the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, because incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes.

Entities: indexer.

Alias: "search-indexer" → "indexer".

Relations? The note mentions "catalog write" — the indexer rebuilds based on catalog writes. Is there a relation between indexer and catalog service? There's an existing fact that the search indexer relies on the catalog service. The note says "instead of on every catalog write" — this implies the indexer depends on the catalog service (writes). Could add a relation depends_on indexer → catalog service. But is that inventing? The note says "on every catalog write" — the indexer previously rebuilt on every catalog write. This does suggest the indexer depends on the catalog. But there's already an existing fact about that dependency. Adding a relation depends_on indexer → catalog service seems reasonable but might be redundant. The instruction says "Add one for each relationship the note states." The note states the indexer rebuilds on catalog writes — that's a dependency relationship between indexer and catalog. Hmm, "catalog write" refers to writes to the catalog, not necessarily the catalog service. I think it's borderline. I'll include depends_on indexer → catalog service? Actually, the note doesn't explicitly say the indexer depends on the catalog service; it says rebuilds happen on catalog writes. The existing memory 1000154 already covers the dependency. I might skip it to avoid inventing. But the relation "rebuilds on every catalog write" is a behavior, not a relation between two entities per se. I'll skip relations, or maybe include depends_on. Let me think.

The safest: add the decision fact, add alias search-indexer → indexer. Possibly no relations. Actually, the note does implicitly connect indexer to catalog writes. But "catalog" isn't an existing entity name; "catalog service" and "product catalog" are. "catalog write" = a write to the product catalog. Hmm. I could add a relation indexer depends_on product catalog? That's speculative. I'll skip.

Should the decision be a correction to any existing fact? Existing facts don't state the rebuild trigger, so no correction.

Fact content: "Decision on 2025-12-18: the indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, because incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes."

Kind: decision. Confidence: 1. Evidence: "search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write, since incremental updates left stale entries behind after failed writes." Shortest quote — maybe "will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write". The evidence should be the shortest span that states this. "search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly instead of on every catalog write" — that covers the decision; the "since" clause covers the reason. I'll use the full sentence minus "Decided in today's standup:".

Entities: ["indexer"].

Alias: name "search-indexer", canonical "indexer", evidence "search-indexer will rebuild the index nightly".

Output JSON only.
